text:
claire: Hi team — customer hitting 504s and high tail latency on /v1/generate yesterday evening. They sent a trace header: trace-id=9f8a7b6c. Time window around 2024-02-10T18:12:00Z to 2024-02-10T18:18:00Z. Can someone pull server-side logs for that trace?

amy: Thanks @claire — can you confirm whether the header was `X-Trace-ID` or `X-Request-Id` in the client? Also if you have the exact client timestamp (ms) that helps. If possible please run this quick repro and drop the raw response: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "X-Trace-ID: 9f8a7b6c" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
```

claire: it was `X-Trace-ID`. attaching the customer's snippet below (they redacted token):
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood-inference.com
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
X-Trace-ID: 9f8a7b6c
Content-Type: application/json
{ "prompt": "long chat...", "max_tokens": 512 }
```

amy: perfect — I'm going to try a quick Kibana search, but FYI retention policy is 30 days for hot logs. If this window is older than that we may need to trigger an archive restore.

ben: FYI from infra side — hot retention is 30 days, cold archive + search is available up to 90 days but requires an export job. If the customer window is ~2024-02-10 it's ~35 days old; likely in cold storage. I can run an ad-hoc export if you confirm start/end in epoch seconds. For quick local check, run this KQL in Kibana: 
```
trace_id: "9f8a7b6c" OR http.request.headers.X-Trace-ID: "9f8a7b6c"
and
@timestamp >= "2024-02-10T18:00:00Z" AND @timestamp <= "2024-02-10T18:30:00Z"
```

dan: If export required, please provide the exact UTC start/end (to the second) and I'll queue `logs-export` with retention copy. Exports need an internal ticket and can take 2-6 hours depending on size. Example export curl (internal):
```
curl -X POST "https://logs-api.internal/v1/exports"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"trace_id":"9f8a7b6c","start_ts":1707618720,"end_ts":1707619080,"reason":"support escalation - customer 1234"}'
```

claire: start_ts ~ 1707618720 end_ts ~ 1707619080 — thanks. Customer can also attach a debug bundle if needed; they asked what to run.

amy: Ask customer to run the debug bundle helper (this will include local headers, timing, and curl output) — paste this (they can redact keys):
```
curl https://support.redwood-inference.com/debug-bundle
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>"
  -F "trace_id=9f8a7b6c"
  -F "timestamp=2024-02-10T18:14:00Z"
```

ben: Export job queued by @dan once internal ticket is created. One more note: because this trace crosses a large request (512 tokens) we should search for large `response_size` spikes and `kv-cache` logs — those are on different shards so include `service:runtime AND trace_id: "9f8a7b6c"` if you need the kernel-level logs.

logbot: Export job 987 queued by dan — ETA 3h. (job-id: export-987) :hourglass: 

amy: Thanks everyone — I'll tell the customer we've queued an export and asked for a debug bundle. Will follow up with results and paste the archive link once ready. :thumbsup:

claire: appreciated — please also include the exact steps you used to search (KQL + time window) so we can replicate for training.

amy: will do, copying KQL + epoch range in the ticket before closing.

dan: assigned to infra for export and I'll attach the result to the support case when ready.

claire: marking resolved on the customer side for now; will re-open if they see more 504s.

amy: closing loop here — follow-up in the ticket with archive link.
